name: Rachel Kim
background: Former McKinsey consultant with two years in the food and beverage strategy practice, advising major QSR chains on expansion and menu strategy. Left to pursue an MBA at Kellogg (specializing in entrepreneurship and marketing), which she completed six months ago. Now launching FreshRoots Kitchen. Has never worked in a restaurant, managed a kitchen, or operated a supply chain. First-time founder with strong analytical skills and genuine passion for the fast-casual space.
personality: Articulate, structured, presents information in frameworks. Leads with market data and financial projections. Impressive on paper and in initial conversation. Struggles when questions move from strategy to operational specifics -- has read extensively but lacks the instincts that come from doing. Compensates with thorough preparation and genuine enthusiasm. Sometimes uses consulting language that signals distance from the operational reality.
motivation: Became obsessed with the fast-casual space while advising a major QSR client at McKinsey and saw what they were doing wrong. Believes she can apply strategic discipline that operators typically lack. Deeply frustrated that operators get the experience but consultants get the analytical edge -- wants to combine both.

capital.embodied_detail: Strong business strategy and financial modeling skills. Genuine knowledge of the fast-casual competitive landscape from an advisory perspective. No operational experience -- has never hired a kitchen manager, negotiated a lease from the operator side, or dealt with a supply chain disruption in real time.
capital.objectified_detail: Detailed market analysis and financial model. Site selection framework built from publicly available data. Letters of interest from two potential franchise partners (sourced through consultancy connections, not direct relationships). No prototype, no revenue.
capital.institutional_detail: Kellogg MBA and McKinsey background are strong signals in consulting and finance circles. Less immediately legible to an operations-focused investor who distinguishes between advising restaurant chains and actually running them.
capital.social_detail: Good network in the consulting and MBA world. Warm introductions through Kellogg alumni network. Limited connections in the restaurant industry itself or among commercial real estate operators.
capital.symbolic_detail: Low symbolic capital in this specific context. An operations-focused investor will immediately notice the gap between her analytical preparation and operational experience. The story is familiar and credible; the protagonist's ability to execute it is not yet established.
